# Psysonic (my own fork)

This is [Psysonic](https://github.com/Psychotoxical/psysonic) with a few small changes. The original README is [here](../README.md).

## What is different

- **Song covers:** everywhere a single song is shown (player bar, Now Playing, queue, fullscreen, song cards, track lists) it shows the song's own embedded cover (`mf-<songId>` on Navidrome) instead of the album cover. See `songOwnCoverEntry` (`src/cover/resolveEntry.ts`) and `usePlaybackTrackCoverRef`. Nine upstream cover tests that expect album covers fail on purpose; they are left untouched to avoid merge conflicts. The settings-backup key test also fails because the fork's own keys (`psysonic_fork_*`) are not in upstream's backup list, for the same reason.
- **Crossfade on skip:** in classic crossfade mode, Next/Previous also fades over the crossfade length (`src/features/playback/utils/playback/autodjManualBlend.ts`).
- **Lyrics stay in sync after a crossfade:** the outgoing track no longer adds its fade-out samples to the shared position counter, which made the new track's position (and synced lyrics) run ahead (`COUNT_EPOCH` in `src-tauri/crates/psysonic-audio/src/sources.rs`).
- **Big albums open faster:** rows outside the view skip layout and paint (`content-visibility` rule at the end of `src/styles/components/tracklist.css`).
- **Discord covers for songs in a shared album:** the Apple artwork lookup also searches by first artist + each part of the song title, and caches per song (`fork_song_search` in `src-tauri/crates/psysonic-integration/src/discord/artwork.rs`).
- **Reverse an album with `#`:** clicking the `#` header flips the album to newest-first, remembered per album; Play, Add to queue and clicking a song follow that order (`useAlbumReversedOrder`, `AlbumDetail.tsx`).
- **No star backdrop:** when an artist has no picture, Navidrome serves its grey star placeholder; the fullscreen player recognises it by its pixels and uses the song's cover as the background instead (`useIsArtistPlaceholder`, `useFsArtistBackdrop.ts`).
- **Animated covers:** a song whose embedded cover is an animated WebP keeps moving. The cover cache normally stores still WebP copies; for an animated source it stores the server's bytes unchanged for every size from 256 px up, while the 128 px list thumbnails stay still (`src-tauri/src/cover_cache/fork_animated.rs`, called from `ensure.rs`).
- **Cover clips:** a song's `<file name>.cover.mp4` from the same server route plays muted and looped over the cover in Now Playing and the fullscreen player, fading in once it plays, so the normal cover always shows first and stays when there is no clip. Kept in `fork-clips` with the background clips, under the same limit; switched by *Animated covers* (`useSongCoverClip`, `ClipVideo`).
- **Faster fullscreen backdrops:** an artist without fanart (or without a MusicBrainz match) is asked again after a week instead of every 30 min / 24 h, and the next song's artist is looked up while the current one plays. A combined artist tag ("BLACKPINK X SELENA GOMEZ") without fanart falls back to the first artist's (`FORK_FANART_MISS_TTL` in `src-tauri/src/cover_cache/external_ensure.rs`, `forkLeadArtist.ts`, `FullscreenPlayerStatic.tsx`).
- **Video backdrop button:** the fullscreen player has a film button next to lyrics that switches *Animated video backdrops* on or off.
- **Background clips:** a song's `<file name>.background.mp4`, served by the server at `/rest/x-clip/<folder>/<file>` behind Navidrome's login, plays muted and looped behind the minimal fullscreen player. Each clip is downloaded once and kept in `fork-clips` in the app data folder (600 MB cap, least recently played removed first, the newest one always kept; a song the clip server answers "no clip" for is remembered for a week, recognised by that server's `Cache-Control` header, while failures are tried again next time). The clip plays over the song's blurred cover. The clip pauses with the music and, by default, while the window is not focused. Settings → Integrations → Fork settings has the switches *Animated covers*, *Animated video backdrops* and *Pause video when Psysonic is not focused*, and a button that clears the kept clips (`src/cover/songClips.ts`, `src/cover/ClipVideo.tsx`, `src-tauri/src/fork_clips.rs`).
- **Fullscreen background never empty:** in the minimal fullscreen player the song's own cover is the background while the fanart.tv lookup runs (it goes through MusicBrainz and can take many seconds) and when the artist has no backdrop, shown at its own size so it never gets blurry (`FullscreenPlayerStatic.tsx`, `fork-clips.css`).
- **Fork settings in one place:** Settings → Integrations → Fork settings holds every setting the fork adds (animated covers and video backdrops, cache size limits, browser cache, offline songs size); the storage ones also stay in Storage, using the same stores so both places stay in sync and lists the fork's changes that have no switch (`ForkSettingsSection.tsx`).
- **Visualizer at 30 fps by default** (upstream 60), and Discord's "External sources only" always searches Apple (`visualizerStore.ts`, `discordPresence.ts`).
- **Old update installers are removed:** each in-app update leaves its installer in `%TEMP%\Psysonic-<version>-updater-*`; the app deletes those folders on start (`src-tauri/src/fork_startup.rs`).
- **Cache size limits and browser cache:** Settings → Storage → Cache size limits sets the cover cache limit (trimmed on start, before the cache opens) and the video backdrop limit (applied at once); Rust keeps them in `fork-settings.json` in the app data folder. The same section shows the webview's own cache (`EBWebView\Default\Cache`, `Code Cache`, `GPUCache`) and clears it through a short restart, since the webview keeps those files open; settings in its storage are kept (`src-tauri/src/fork_startup.rs`, `ForkCacheLimitsSection.tsx`).
- **Offline songs size in Storage:** Settings → Storage → Media folder shows how much the offline songs take (`ForkOfflineSize.tsx`).
- **Updates come from this fork:** the in-app update check reads this fork's releases (`src/features/updater`). `src-tauri/fork.conf.json` swaps in this fork's updater key and feed at build time.

## How releases happen

The **Fork sync and release** workflow runs every day. When upstream's `release` branch has a version this fork hasn't released, it merges that version into `main` inside the runner (nothing is pushed), builds the Windows installer, signs it and publishes `fork-vX.Y.Z` with upstream's release notes added below the fork's own lines. The app then offers the update. It can also be run by hand with **force** to rebuild the current version.

## If a run fails

Usually upstream changed the same lines as a patch. If only version and lock files conflict (`package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `tauri.conf.json`, `flake.lock`, ...), the fork never changes them: take upstream's side (`git checkout --theirs`). Merge `upstream/release` into `main` locally, fix the conflict, push, then run the workflow by hand.

- **Branch:** `main` is the default branch, based on upstream `release` (stable versions only). New work goes on its own branch and is merged into `main` when it is done.
- **Signing key:** repo secrets `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`. The public half is in `src-tauri/fork.conf.json`. If the key is lost, generate a new one, update both places and reinstall once by hand, because installed copies only accept updates signed with the old key.
